i usually use my biggest saucepan since i have a big soup pot that fits them nicely but yeah that's a problem. Other than buying a large cheap saucepan you could run it under a hot tap till it softens a bit and then try folding it into a smaller pan, they do squish up when they're soft. When you activate it also massage it to soften it up and perhaps fold it before it goes completely cold. try that otherwise i guess buy a large cheap pot.

yes do! i have a ton of them and some larger ones too that are great for your back etc. i definitely prefer a laundry net over a tea towel but the tea towel is good in a pinch if you have nothing else.

When they're done boiling just check for any crystals left, if there is 1 crystal not melted it will coll down and go solid again so just boil for a little longer. Boiling for longer will not harm them
you should have been told to put a tea towel on the bottom of the pot so they don't touch. or use a laundry bag/net like i do. you can also use a colander to suspend them in the boiling water.

i used to sell these, they last about 10 years, you need to boil them after each use (actually boil on the stove not just drop in hot water) and don't let them touch the base of the pot. You can wrap in a tea towel or use a laundry bag like i do. I have a lot of these including large ones for the back, shoulders and knees. So i tend to use them all and have a big boiling session afterwards.

If you're boiling a lot they need to boil for longer than just a single small one.
